body:
# Independent audit: radial layer barrier strictification

Audited source: `candidate 5276d0526911b81d`.


interior section is an explicit hypothesis, and the conclusion is
a strictification and cap-budget preservation tool, not an OC bound.
The companion exact verifier is
`supporting computation verify_radial_layer_barrier_strictification_functional.py`.

## 1. The finite representation barrier, including equation (5)

For a nonvertex z of conv(P), the excluded-target representation
polytope A_z is nonempty and compact. Its finitely many vertices
have finitely many positive coordinates, so their minimum alpha_*
is strictly positive. No assertion about a minimum positive
coefficient over ALL representations is being made; that assertion
would be false and is not used.

When z is removed at layer ell>=1, it is a vertex of the hull of
the then remaining set. An excluded-target representation using
only that set would contradict this vertex property. Hence every
such representation, in particular every extreme one, uses an
earlier-layer point with positive coefficient.

After the affine section is sheared to zero, all support values
h_p(u) lie in [m,M], uniformly over every unit direction. Thus
H=sum alpha_p h_p(u) also lies in [m,M], and the normalized
earlier-layer support weight alpha_p h_p(u)/H is at least
alpha_* m/M >= delta. If its actual weight is larger than delta,
replacing the excess by weight at the maximal barrier value only
increases the proposed upper bound. Therefore equation (5) is
valid, with the exact calculation

    delta(1-delta^(ell-1))+(1-delta)(1-delta^L)
      =1-delta^ell-(1-delta)delta^L=b_z-kappa.

Multiplication by H gives a gain H kappa>=m kappa. The compatibility
support inequality h_z-H>=0 then gives (4) and (6). This handles
representations using later layers, a case where merely ordering
the layer indices without normalized support weights would not
suffice.

An arbitrary point of A_z is a convex combination of its extreme
points. The support gap is affine in that representation vector,
so the SAME uniform gap extends to all excluded-target
representations. This is a valid finite-polytope argument; it
does not assume direction-independent supporting faces.

## 2. Self weights, perturbations, and exact fibers

A representation with self weight theta<1 reduces to an excluded
representation by dividing the other weights by 1-theta. This
is valid because the resulting barycenter is still z. The gap for
the original representation is scaled by 1-theta and need not be
uniform as theta approaches one. The source correctly claims
uniform strictness only after excluding the target's self weight.
It uses the self-weight step solely to recover compatibility.

The common mass-normalizing factor lambda is positive and tends
to one. It preserves every support inequality, multiplies the
strict gap by lambda, and gives exactly the required total volume
through its d-th power. Returning through the affine shear gives
homotheties about q(z), rather than about unrelated centers.

For independent Hausdorff perturbations, the support loss at a
target is at most eta and the weighted source support gain is at
most eta; there is no missing factor depending on the number of
fibers. Thus g-2eta is the correct uniform lower bound. The
inradius condition keeps every perturbed fiber full-dimensional.
For any slice of the convex hull, grouping the hull coefficients
by base and using compatibility gives inclusion in its prescribed
fiber; the opposite inclusion is immediate. Lattice completeness
then excludes new integer bases. The asserted body interior is
correctly relative to aff(P) times R^d unless the base span is full.

If P has no nonvertices, the note separately avoids defining
alpha_* and correctly observes that independent small perturbations
already preserve the exact vertex fibers.

## 3. Exact budget scope

For a hyperplane through the whole affine section q, a positive
radial dilation about q(z) preserves each fiber's cap FRACTION.
It does not generally preserve its absolute cap mass. When this
fraction is the same p_u at every base, summing after the common
total-volume normalization yields exactly p_u W, as claimed.
The same argument applies to any number of such directions,
including an infinite collection. The normal u is nonzero, so
the continuous hyperplane has zero d-volume in every full fiber.

The note explicitly excludes caps with another offset and
directions with unequal fractions. It also does not assume that
an affine interior section always exists. These restrictions are
necessary; the examples below independently test them.

## 4. Rational nonhomothetic example with all central budgets preserved

Use bases 0,1,2 and centered planar bodies

    K0=[-1,1]^2,
    K2={|x1|+|x2|<=2},
    K1=(K0+K2)/2.

The middle body has vertices
(3/2,1/2),(1/2,3/2),(-1/2,3/2),(-3/2,1/2) and their negatives.
Their areas are 4,7,8. These three shapes are not homothetic.
The only excluded-target relation is K1=(K0+K2)/2, so the family
is actually compatible. All contain the unit Euclidean ball,
and their support values are at most 2 on unit directions.

Thus m=1,M=2, alpha_*=1/2, delta=1/4, b1=3/4 and
kappa=3/16. Choose epsilon=64/831. The expansion factors are
1,293/277,1 and the exact mass-normalizing factor is 277/283.
The final radial factors are

    (s0,s1,s2)=(277/283,293/283,277/283),
    12(277/283)^2+7(293/283)^2=19.

In particular every final vertex remains rational. The actual
excluded-middle support gap is (16/283)h_K1>=16/283; the theorem's
certified common gap is the valid smaller number g=4/283.
For example eta=1/566 satisfies both required strict bounds for
the independent perturbation neighborhood.

All bodies are centrally symmetric about zero. Hence every
through-zero directional cap has fraction1/2 at every base, and
ALL such original budgets remain exactly 19/2 after strictification.
This example checks arbitrary shapes, exact normalization, and
simultaneous preservation without homothety of the original bodies.

## 5. Rational noncentral shapes and an oblique affine section

In centered coordinates use

    K0=[-1,1]^2,
    K2=conv{(-2,-1),(2,-1),(0,2)},
    K1=(K0+K2)/2.

The middle hexagon has vertices
(-3/2,-1),(3/2,-1),(3/2,0),(1/2,3/2),(-1/2,3/2),(-3/2,0).
The respective areas are 4,6,6, and the total is16. Each body
contains the unit ball; the triangle's sloping facets are at
distance4/sqrt(13)>1 from zero. Support values are at most3.
Thus take m=1,M=3, delta=1/6, b1=5/6 and kappa=5/36.

Choose epsilon=12/43. Expansion followed by exact normalization
gives the rational factors

    (s0,s1,s2)=(43/47,53/47,43/47),
    10(43/47)^2+6(53/47)^2=16.

The certified gap is g=5/141, and the actual gap is at least10/47.
The choice eta=1/200 is safely within the claimed neighborhood.

Now translate fiber z by the AFFINE section q(z)=(z,2z-1).
The ambient plane x1-z=0 passes through this section and cuts
each fiber in half by its reflection symmetry in the first
continuous coordinate. Its total cap budget therefore remains
exactly8, although the bodies are not centrally symmetric and
are not homothetic.

By contrast, the direction x2-(2z-1)>=0 has original fiber
fractions 1/2,1/2,4/9. Its original budget is23/3. The new budget
is exactly

    23/3+120/2209,

so it is NOT preserved. This verifies that equality of the
per-fiber fractions is substantive, rather than a dispensable
condition hidden by the normalization.

## 6. Multi-layer check and final scope

The verifier additionally uses P={-2,-1,0,1,2} and
K_z=[-1,1]^2+(4-z^2){|x1|+|x2|<=1}. Concavity of 4-z^2 gives
all compatibility relations. Its peeling depths are0,1,2,1,0,
and every extreme excluded-target representation is enumerated
exactly as a two-point representation. Here alpha_*=1/4; with
m=1,M=6 the construction has delta=1/24 and
kappa=23/13824. All earlier-layer weights, barrier inequalities,
and mixtures with nonzero self weights are checked exactly.

The finite checks supplement the proof-level audit above. No
claim about arbitrary-shape cap Hessians, automatic affine-section
existence, intrinsic direction changes, or an OC improvement is
added by this audit.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
